sections.heading: Three choices shape your quote.
sections.text:
Three choices shape your quote.
The model, the scope and the work. Pick each one, and the quote follows.
1
Which model?
Model
How the job is contracted. EPCC: IAQ delivers everything and answers for the result. EPCM: the owner holds the contracts and IAQ manages them. A single service on its own. Or, for energy, an ESCO contract paid from the savings.
2
Which scope?
Service
What the contract covers. One of the six services, several, or all six. For example procurement only, design only, or design, procure and build.
3
Which work?
Work
Which kind of work the contractor does, which is how the market classifies it: CSA, MEP or process utilities. Most contractors do one. IAQ does all three in house.

Choosing a model
How IAQ is engaged, and who answers for what.
4
Which model should I choose?
EPCC when you want one party to deliver everything and answer for the result. EPCM when you hold the construction contracts yourself and want IAQ to manage them. Large multinationals engage EPCM on the biggest programmes.
See EPC
→
What is the difference between EPCC and EPCM?
EPCC is EPC plus Commissioning: IAQ delivers the whole project, commissioning included. EPCM is EPC Management: IAQ manages the project to the same standard, and the owner holds the construction contracts.
Can I buy one service on its own?
Yes. Procurement only, design only, or design, procure and construct. The scope changes; the EPC model still governs how it runs.
Who answers for a system’s performance?
Under EPCC, IAQ: one contract, one party, from the first drawing to a facility proven to operate as intended. Under EPCM the owner holds the contracts and IAQ manages them; the standard the work is held to is the same.
Time and cost
How long each engagement runs, and what is paid when.
4
How long does a facility take?
Typically 12 to 24 months under EPC, depending on the project. Tool hookup is priced and scheduled per tool set.
How is tools hookup priced?
Per tool set. Each set is scoped from the tool maker’s facility requirements, so the price follows the tools you bring in, not the size of the fab.
See PCU & TTI
→
What does an energy contract cost up front?
Nothing. Under Cooling as a Service IAQ funds, builds and runs the chiller plant for a fixed tariff over 10 to 20 years. Under Energy Performance Contracting IAQ funds the upgrade and is paid from the measured savings over 5 to 10 years.
See EFM
→
How are the savings measured?
Against an audited baseline agreed before the work starts. IAQ is paid from the measured saving, so the saving has to be real and has to last.
